source_locator.description: Opening parenthetical immediately after the canonical scene-1 heading.

translation.english_text: (As Kalyani's wedding is about to take place in Madurai, her three elder brothers—Chandrasekaran, Gnanasekaran and Gunasekaran—are in Rangoon. At that time, in Madurai... a dance is taking place at a gathering.)
notes: The three personal names are transliterated; the source relationship `அண்ணன்மார்கள்` is rendered as `elder brothers`.

source_locator.description: Parenthetical after the opening song and immediately before Thangappan's speech.

translation.english_text: (When the dance and songs end, the bridegroom speaks.)

(Respected elders, until now you have enjoyed the voice of the new mingled with a new kind of dance. The children of such a beautiful land, instead of crawling in the lap of this Mother Earth, go away to other countries. When I think of this, I remember something one of our thinkers said. If we were to give an imaginative reason for why seawater is salty... he said it is because of the tears shed by Tamils who, unable to make a living in their own land, went abroad. Why go that far? Here is Kalyani, whom I am about to marry: she has apparently never even seen the faces of her brothers! They left for Rangoon when she was so young. And not only they! Hundreds of thousands of young people. Countless families! In Malaya's rubber plantations! In Africa, on the island of Ceylon—they must all return to our cherished homeland. That is exactly what this beautiful song reminds us of.)
